headline: Medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks from shared text/audio pipelines; no direct evidence of a blocking control.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content and agent-protocol inputs, while pipecat moves text through shared-bus/session pipelines and stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if AutoGPT consumes pipecat outputs as trusted text. No direct provenance or isolation controls are documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF pipecat output is copied into AutoGPT prompts or files without provenance tags, injection is possible.
IF both agents share a bus, clipboard, or workspace, attacker-controlled text can traverse the boundary.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before AutoGPT ingests pipecat text.
Prefix all inter-agent messages with immutable provenance labels.
Disable automatic file ingestion for shared outputs.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
requires-engineering: add content filtering and instruction-stripping at the handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; pipecat handles text, audio, video, images, and conversation state over shared-bus/session state. If sensitive content enters pipecat, it can be forwarded into AutoGPT outputs or external APIs. The profiles do not show explicit data-class restrictions, so a shared-workspace leakage path is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive text or media is placed on the shared bus, AutoGPT may read it from files or prompts.
IF AutoGPT forwards that content to an allowlisted API, the data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of the shared bus.
Use separate OS users and directories for each agent.
Turn off AutoGPT access to shared folders.
Review outbound destinations in AutoGPT allowlists.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and pipecat supports multiple instances with shared-bus state. Even without explicit write scopes, both can mutate shared files or runtime state if orchestrated together. Because locking or coordination is not documented, the overlap is enough for a default conflict risk rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or config files, state races can occur.
IF the orchestrator lacks locks, concurrent subprocesses can clobber shared artifacts.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Run only one writer at a time.
Keep pipecat state in memory-only mode where possible.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can pass conversation state and text through its pipeline, and AutoGPT can act on that text via shell or API calls. If AutoGPT-generated content is treated as authoritative by pipecat components, errors can cascade into downstream actions or user-facing speech. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is inferred and should be treated as medium.
conditions: IF pipecat forwards AutoGPT output directly into downstream actions, mistakes propagate.
IF AutoGPT hallucinates facts and pipecat speaks or routes them without verification, users receive false outputs.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before pipecat acts on AutoGPT output.
Require human approval for any action-taking branch.
Limit AutoGPT to drafting, not executing, in the shared flow.
Log and diff outputs before downstream use.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for all inter-agent messages.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention commitments. The only concrete compliance signal is pipecat's analytics/metrics and third-party service integrations, while AutoGPT exposes allowlisted egress. Because no specific regulated data class or jurisdiction mismatch is documented, this is a documented-gap risk rather than a stronger breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through pipecat analytics or external STT/LLM/TTS services, policy review is required.
IF the deployment has residency or retention requirements, the current profiles do not document compliance controls.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair.
Disable analytics where possible.
Review third-party service destinations.
Document retention settings before deployment.
requires-engineering: add jurisdiction-aware routing and retention controls.
